Health

Report liveness, API version, and the running commit hash.

Ninja injects the request positionally; it is unused here but must be named without a leading underscore so the schema generator does not treat it as a request-body field.

/api/health

Content type
application/json

}

Signup

Create/attach a fan from a verified OTP + consent; issue a token pair.

Delivery follows the requested surface (ADR-0002): the web flow gets hardened httpOnly cookies (no token in the body); the app gets the tokens in the body.

Request Body schema: application/json
required
phone
required
string (Phone)
otp_code
required
string (Otp Code)
nickname
required
string (Nickname) [ 1 .. 40 ] characters
consent_terms
required
boolean (Consent Terms)
consent_privacy
required
boolean (Consent Privacy)
web
boolean (Web)
Default: false

Responses

/api/fan/signup

Request samples

  • Payload
Content type

  • "otp_code": "string",
  • "nickname": "string",

}

Record Consent

Record one scope's portrait-rights consent (manager+).

The rights gate is manager-gated: operators ready a profile, a manager grants what fans may see, reflecting that cast consent is not an operator decision.

Authorizations:
RoleRequired
path Parameters
cast_id
required
string <uuid> (Cast Id)
Request Body schema: application/json
required
scope
required
string (Scope) <= 32 characters
status
required
string (Status) <= 16 characters
note
string (Note) <= 255 characters
Default: ""

Responses

/api/cast/profiles/{cast_id}/consent

    },
  • "created_at": "2019-08-24T14:15:22Z"
}

View Public Cast Profile

Read the consent-gated public view as a fan; records an impression.

FanBearerAuth is role-agnostic, so a FAN role is required (a staff token must not be logged as a fan impression — the cast_profile_viewed metric would be polluted; mirrors the ASS-110 fan gate). A hidden or unconsented profile 404s so its existence is not disclosed.

Authorizations:
FanBearerAuth
path Parameters
cast_id
required
string <uuid> (Cast Id)

Responses

/api/cast/public-profiles/{cast_id}

Response samples

  • 200
  • 403
  • 404
Content type
application/json
{
  • "cast_id": "string",
  • "stage_name": "string",
  • "intro": "string",
  • "photo_ref": "string",
  • "schedule_visible": true,
  • "cheki_available": true,
  • "content_scope": "string"
}

operator-metrics

Get Metrics

Return the MSFC/rate/guardrail KPIs for a window and log the view.

The window is the half-open [start, end); both default to the current calendar month (start/end each fall back to the month of whichever bound — or today — is given). The view is audited (dashboard_viewed, target operator_metrics) so weekly KPI usage is countable.

Authorizations:
RoleRequired
query Parameters
Start (string) or Start (null) (Start)
End (string) or End (null) (End)

Responses

Create Fan Report

File a safety report as the authenticated fan (ASS-110, F11).

Bearer-only on purpose. This is a state-changing POST, and the fan cookie surface (ADR-0002 web httpOnly cookies) needs CSRF protection for unsafe methods — the double-submit defense ASS-98 deferred to "the first authenticated state-changing fan endpoint". Rather than ship a CSRF-exposed cookie path (an auth/session concern, CONSTRAINTS #26 human-gated), v0 accepts only the bearer token (the app surface, which browsers do not auto-send, so it is not CSRF- prone). Web-cookie reporting lands with the CSRF work. The endpoint issues no tokens, so it stays an ordinary business endpoint, not auth code.

The fan is recorded as the reporter, severity is server-derived from the type, and the narrative goes only to the restricted store.

Authorizations:
FanBearerAuth
Request Body schema: application/json
required
report_type
required
string (Report Type) <= 64 characters
narrative
string (Narrative) <= 2000 characters
Default: ""

Responses

/api/safety/fan-reports

  • "report_type": "string",

}

  • "status": "string",

}

Get Handling Stats

Report-handling operations metrics for the operator triage queue (ASS-111).

Completes the "신고 ... 처리 시간 집계" workflow on top of the ASS-96 lifecycle: the open queue by status/severity, the oldest unresolved age, and how many reports were resolved in the trailing window_days with their median/mean handling time. Counts + durations only — never narrative or PII. Operator+, matching the report list (these are triage figures, not restricted detail).
